# The Masonry Modeler

> Masonry estimating software that counts fulls, halves, and corners from the first click as you draw your walls. The model renders the pieces and carries their counts into the material list, estimate, and shop drawings. Built by a mason because existing tools count masonry walls like carpet (length × height × factor) instead of modeling them as bonded units. Demos are available by request. Founder pricing is $300 per seat per month for the first 10 companies; contact Ryan for current availability.

## Background

The Masonry Modeler (TMM) is built by Ryan Shanley of Powder River Masonry. The thesis: a masonry wall is not a rectangular field of units to be divided and multiplied. It is a bonded assembly where corners interlock, bond beams wrap, lintels land on specific courses, and non-modular heights produce half-high courses that need their own SKU. Every existing tool treats masonry as a rectangle-counting problem. TMM models the bond first and counts the bond's consequences.

## Core technical rules the engine enforces

- Corners interlock by default; the bond runs through them, inside and outside
- Non-modular leftover is absorbed into the corner — the leg moves 8 inches every course, same as the bond
- Control joints default to 24 feet 8 inches (296 inches = 18.5 blocks × 16 inches exactly); never auto-placed within 16 inches of a corner
- Bond beam courses are driven by the rebar schedule from the structural drawings, not by a checkbox
- Half-high courses are generated and broken out as their own line item, not buried in a waste factor
- Review small closures at tight openings, corners, and special details in the elevation and cutting list
- 10-inch and 12-inch CMU corners are listed as an 8-inch block plus a face shell spacer (separate line items, the way the supplier ships them)
- Every block-by-block decision is overridable by the mason — one click changes the unit, takeoff updates immediately
- Shop drawings are a byproduct of the model: one trace produces coursed, tagged elevations (numbered courses, grout lifts, openings, finishes, control joints) plus a rebar/dowel layout and a steel bar list — every bar counted by mark and cut length with corner-bend and peak-bend shape codes, not linear feet with a waste factor

## Video proof

A three-minute screen recording of the 88th Avenue pump station being traced and taken off in The Masonry Modeler is embedded on the How It Works page, the CMU Block Count page, and the Masonry Takeoff Accuracy page. Hosted on YouTube: https://youtu.be/m-fSK2uB924

## Pages

### The job (one page per headache)
- [Home](https://themasonrymodeler.com/): The estimator on an island: every wall, every piece, every special shape counted by wall and lift before you sign; live 3-D demo of a real pump station job; send us your next bid
- [Estimating](https://themasonrymodeler.com/estimating/): Draw the wall once; TMM lays every block, cut, corner and bar up the gable and around the openings. On our own gabled brick job, within 0.2% of our Bluebeam count
- [Field](https://themasonrymodeler.com/field/): The crew's Story Pole link: tap a wall, pick a lift, check off block, rebar and grout, drag for a partial lift, View in AR on iPhone/iPad
- [Changes](https://themasonrymodeler.com/changes/): One model, not four documents: takeoff, bar list, shop drawings and the crew's link all come from the one model; IFC exports carry a revision stamp
- [Schedule](https://themasonrymodeler.com/schedule/): Day-by-day plan from the block count: lay the lift, sit overnight, grout, go up. Crew-from-deadline and plan-vs-actual are coming
- [How It Works & Pricing](https://themasonrymodeler.com/how-it-works/): Worked estimate, screenshots, how the count is built, shop drawing, comparison, founder pricing, FAQ

### Architectural (product / topic pages)
- [CMU Block Count](https://themasonrymodeler.com/cmu-block-count/): CMU quantity review and a worked estimate with explicit sample material, labor, equipment, overhead, and profit inputs
- [Bond Beam Estimating](https://themasonrymodeler.com/bond-beam-estimating/): Rebar-driven bond beam scheduling with continuous corner wraps and rebar weight in pounds
- [Masonry Takeoff Accuracy](https://themasonrymodeler.com/masonry-takeoff-accuracy/): The three repeating sources of takeoff error — lintels, corners, half-block courses — and how to eliminate them
- [Masonry Shop Drawings](https://themasonrymodeler.com/masonry-shop-drawings/): Submittal-ready coursed, tagged elevations rendered as you build — openings, special shapes, finishes, bond beams, control joints — plus a rebar/dowel layout and a steel bar list (285 bars, 2,031.4 LF on the sample 15th pod set) counted by mark and cut length. Downloadable 9-sheet sample set.
- [CMU Takeoff Software](https://themasonrymodeler.com/cmu-takeoff-software/): How to take off CMU from the bond — units instead of net area, corners and bullnose by course, halves and cuts, bond beams and lintels, vertical rebar with laps, and grout by cell
- [Brick Takeoff Software](https://themasonrymodeler.com/brick-takeoff-software/): How to take off brick veneer from the actual bond — openings, corners, soldier and rowlock courses, and brick over block

### Field Notes (blog)
- [Blog Index](https://themasonrymodeler.com/blog/)
- [Why I Built The Masonry Modeler](https://themasonrymodeler.com/blog/why-i-built-this/): Founder story — the Douglas Humane Society job where the rectangle-counter model became impossible to ignore
- [The Software Sees the Corner. Why Am I Placing It?](https://themasonrymodeler.com/blog/software-sees-the-corner/): On automatic corner detection, the cost premium of corner SKUs, and the half-high-course miss
- [The Corner Test](https://themasonrymodeler.com/blog/the-corner-test/): A one-minute test — draw two walls meeting at a corner — that shows whether a tool models bonded masonry or just rectangles
- [Half the Block, Two-Thirds the Price](https://themasonrymodeler.com/blog/half-block-cost/): A half block costs about two-thirds of a full one; missing the half-block count shorts the bid in the one direction you can't claw back
- [We All Label Shop Drawings in Bluebeam by Hand. Why?](https://themasonrymodeler.com/blog/bluebeam-shop-drawings/): The export-and-annotate workflow re-types labels the model already knew — the drawing should label itself
- [What Goes On a Masonry Shop Drawing](https://themasonrymodeler.com/blog/whats-on-a-masonry-shop-drawing/): What the coursed submittal has to show — coursing, special shapes, openings, reinforcing, control joints — and why the contractor has to produce it
- [Drawing Masonry in SketchUp](https://themasonrymodeler.com/blog/masonry-shop-drawings-in-sketchup/): Why building masonry shop drawings in SketchUp by hand is so much work — the model doesn't know it's a wall
- [Stop Guessing Your Half Block Order](https://themasonrymodeler.com/blog/stop-guessing-half-block-order/): The 20% rule breaks on modern jobs that mix bullnose, split-face, colors, and multiple widths — "halves" isn't one line item anymore
- [What Skipping the Shop Drawing Costs You](https://themasonrymodeler.com/blog/what-skipping-the-shop-drawing-costs/): On one recent job the sheets totalled 12,624 units and the order was 11,485 — the 1,139-unit gap was corners counted twice, caught by one line of reconciliation
- [Stop Paying for Masonry Shop Drawings](https://themasonrymodeler.com/blog/stop-paying-for-masonry-shop-drawings/): The takeoff already paid for the shop drawings; TMM prints the coursed set from the same model that priced the job — no per-sheet fees, no re-draft on revisions
- [A Masonry Shop Drawing Example, Read Line by Line](https://themasonrymodeler.com/blog/masonry-shop-drawing-example/): One real CMU rake-wall elevation — courses C1–C30 over a curb, lift lines every six courses, vertical and bond beam steel with laps, solid grout hatch, banded block colors, rake cuts — and what each mark means

## About the founder

Ryan Shanley is the founder of Powder River Masonry and the builder of The Masonry Modeler. He does masonry takeoffs by hand in spreadsheets because the available estimating tools do not model masonry. TMM is the tool he wanted and could not find.
